newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan auto parts makers abandon China venture plan.
newsitem.headline: Japan auto parts makers abandon China venture plan.

text.p: Japanese auto parts makers Aisin Seiki Co Ltd and Unisia Jecs Corp said on Friday they had abandoned plans to form a venture to make clutches with China's Yuejin Motor Corp.
Aisin and Unisia Jecs started negotiations with Yuejin Motor over forming the venture in China in 1995 but decided to abandon the plans late last year, an Aisin spokesman said.
Both companies said they were worried about lack of demand after talks between Nissan Motor Co Ltd and a Chinese company on producing engines for small trucks in Nanjing broke down in November.
In March, French car parts maker Valeo signed a joint venture agreement with Yuejin Motor to make clutches.
Aisin is owned 22.6 percent by Toyota Motor Corp while Unisia Jecs is owned 29.5 percent by Nissan Motor and 10.1 percent by Robert Bosch GmbH.
